chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Hello and welcome to this lecture series on microprocessor and microcontroller.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And in this current video, we are going to discuss 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And we are going to discuss the pin diagram of 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: In the earlier video lecture, that is video lecture number 11,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: we have studied the architecture of 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So let me just quickly revise what we did in the last lecture.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in the last lecture, we have seen one slide for architecture.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So for 8086 microprocessor, the architecture is this.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the main highlights of this architecture in comparison to the 8085 microprocessor was

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: that bus interface unit and execution unit are separate here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean, execution unit will all deal with execution of the statements that we have made in programming,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: the arithmetic, shift statements, etc.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: These calculations will be done by the execution unit.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the bus interface unit, it will be working independent of this execution unit.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the purpose of bus execution unit will be to transfer the data from the externally interfaced

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: one megabyte memory.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That is the maximum possible memory, which you can externally interface to 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So it's not that 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that's why every location in the memory will also be of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: No.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Every location in the memory that is externally interfaced memory will still be of 8 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That is 1 byte.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And we will have 1 mega such locations.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That is 2 raised to the power of 20 such locations.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And since 8086 happens to be a 16-bit microprocessor, which means that the data bus that you see here,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: it's of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: However, the address bus has to be of 20 bits because 2 raised to the power of 20 is 1 mega.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that is why we can address the externally interfaced 1 megabyte memory locations there.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And on that note, we have most of the general purpose registers, which are accumulator, B register,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: C register, D register, etc.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: These are all 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: However, they can also be used in this 8-bit fashion, the higher byte and the lower order byte.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So they can be used in that fashion also.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then you have got stack pointer, then base pointer, source index, destination index, etc.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: In this execution unit.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: These registers that you see here, code segment, data segment, extra segment, stack segment,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: and instruction pointer.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: They are also of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But they contain the address of the corresponding sections in the externally interfaced memory.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: For example, code segment in externally interfaced memory, which is 1 megabyte completely, will be of 64 kilobyte.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Similarly, if you talk about data segment, it will also be of 64 kilobytes.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Extra segment and stack segment will also be of 64 kilobytes each.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this code segment, it will contain the starting address of that particular code segment in the externally interfaced memory.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now you will ask the question that since the externally interfaced memory can be addressed by 20 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So how is it possible that the code segment, which is inside this microprocessor, this code segment register is of 16 bits?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So we said that the beginning address has to be such that the last four bits have to be zero.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It is by default like that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that is why since the last four bits are zero, that is why 16 bits are left.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So those 16 bits will be kept in code segment, data segment, extra segment and stack segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Instruction pointer we have discussed.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It's like the program counter in 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We will talk about it more when we will do the programming.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We have a separate instruction queue here, which is of six bytes.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in advance, this 8086 microprocessor can contain six bytes of the code that we have written.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And when this queue has two empty locations, in that case only, the next two bytes will be fetched.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Not before that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this is how this 8086 performs.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And this bus interface unit and execution unit is independent of each other.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the fetch, execute and decode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This three phase cycle, fetch, execute and decode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: These three are independent of each other.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Otherwise, in 8085, what used to happen was, we usually take one byte from the externally interface memory,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: keep it in the instruction register, decode it and then execute it.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then we take the next byte, etc.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But here we try to fetch six bytes at max in advance.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that's what happens in 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So let me first check whether this video is getting recorded or not.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Yeah, it's getting recorded.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So after that, after this architecture part, these were the main highlights of this architecture.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And now in this today's session, we are going to discuss the pin diagram of this 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, this is a 40 pin IC.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: There are 40 pins here, as you can see on the slide.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This starts from one and go up to 40 here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And let me first just tell you how to switch on this 8086 CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So for that, you have obviously this VCC, which is the 40th pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And this VCC can be plus 5 volts and the tolerance limit is 10%, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Plus minus 10% could be the variation.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this VCC has to be supplied with a DC voltage of plus 5 volts.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: In that case, it will be on.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now you can see that there are two ground pins here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This is the one ground pin, which is on pin number one.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And on pin number 20, you can also see that there is a ground signal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So now, why two grounds are there in one IC?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So what happens is when you have a bigger circuit,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: when you have a bigger circuit, then you will require multiple grounds.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because what happens is suppose if this pin is suppose high,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: then a pin is high or low with respect to the ground pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So there are these two ground pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So if the ground voltage is treated as zero,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: then plus 5 volt will be treated as a high volt,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: high or logic one at this particular pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So these two have to be internally connected through some resistance,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which will let you know that this point has a potential of plus 5 volt.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But what happens is there are multiple number of pins in this integrated circuit.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this ground, which is supposed to be zero ideally does not remain zero.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It also acquires certain kind of voltage because of these multiple pins being grounded to the same pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that is why to keep the ground voltage at zero absolutely,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: we have got these two pins here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the details of this might have been known to you from your electronics circuit code,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: the basic electronics code, where you also learn that in a big circuit,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: you have to have multiple number of grounds.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So because of that reason only you have got multiple grounds here, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this VCC and these two ground pins,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: they have to be appropriately placed VCC at plus 5 volt,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: plus 5 volt DC battery.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And then at ground pins, you have to give the ground signal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That is, you have to ground them.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And then you have to provide a clock here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That clock, we have already discussed how the clock should be.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: The frequency is 5 MHz for the base variant of 8086 CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the duty cycle has to be 33%.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Means in every period of that clock pulse,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: it should remain on for 33% of the time.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that way this clock signal has to be provided, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So if you, if you apply all these signals, your microprocessor will become on, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now you see two things here, maximum mode and minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I think we have already had a discussion about this maximum mode and minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So by minimum mode, what we mean is,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: if the microprocessor is the only processor that is present in the circuit.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that's what we mean by minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the signals that you see in brackets here,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: they are all applicable to minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And maximum mode means the mode in which there are multiple processors,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which are connected in the system, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that mode is called as maximum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the signals that you see here, which are not written in any bracket,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: they are for maximum mode, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So at one particular time,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: this microprocessor can either operate in minimum or operate in maximum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It cannot operate in both of the modes at the same time.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So you have to select one particular mode of operation.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So based upon that, the meaning of these pins will be taken.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: You can see that there are some double meanings,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which are written for these pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, these two meanings will depend upon whether the microprocessor operates

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: in maximum mode or minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And which will,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: how will we know that our processor is operating in maximum or minimum mode?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So for that, we have a pin here,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: MN slash MX bar, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So if this pin is set as high,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: then it is operating in the minimum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And if this pin is set as low,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: then it is operating in the maximum mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that's what we mean by this minimum and maximum mode of operation here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in this diagram,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I haven't shown the directional nature of these pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So I will explain them as I carry forward my explanation, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the minimum and maximum mode, I guess, is clear to everyone.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If there are multiple processors in the system.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, one question, one very natural question could be,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: why would someone like to have multiple processors in their computer?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So think about a situation as we have seen in 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: There was, there were only this addition and subtraction commands.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: No multiplication command, no division command,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: no command for taking the logarithm of something,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: no command for taking the sinusoidal of something.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So these commands were not there.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So for these, you have to write programs inside 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Similarly in 8086 CPU,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: you will see that there will be command for addition,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: subtraction, multiplication, and division as well,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which were not there in 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in 8085,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: multiplication and division were not there,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: but here they will be there.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But still, in today's world,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: we know that we frequently use this logarithm operation,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: sine operation, tan operation,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: and there are other mathematical functions which are frequently used.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So we do not write programs for that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We can directly just use our scientific calculators,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which is provided in our machines,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: and we can just do things with that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, since these commands are very less,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which are present in this 8086 CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in that case, you know,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: there is something which is called as a math co-processor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: The math co-processor can be used with this processor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Co-processor because it will operate together with this processor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that processor is 8087.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This is 8086.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And you can have one more processor,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: which will have dedicated operations for mathematics.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That processor is called as 8087 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And it operates together with this CPU as the main CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So you can have multiple processors in the system.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And it's not because that three or four people who have got 8086 computer,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: they are trying to connect with each other.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And that is the only reason that we are having multiple processors in the system.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It's not like that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Processors, they do different tasks.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This 8086 is a general purpose CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It can be used for any purpose.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It is not that we cannot implement a program which won't be able to perform sign function.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It can do that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But there is a separate dedicated processor for that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So 8086, sorry, 8087 is called as math co-processor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So still in 8086, you will see that we have a hundred mnemonics.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We have about a hundred mnemonics here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And there are combinations that we can make.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: There are combinations that we can make are 3,800.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: About 3,800 combinations would be made.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: In 8085, we had 74 instructions.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And there, I think 243 combinations can be made.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: However, in this 8086 CPU, we have got 100 instructions.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: About 100 instructions.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And 3,800 combinations can be made.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And out of those 3,800 combinations, you can make various permutations and combinations

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: and write your program.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the instruction set of this 8086 CPU is very powerful as compared to 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We will see that in our programming sessions.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So now let me just begin by explaining each and every pin to you.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Each and every pin that you see here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Let us try to just elaborate on that part.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So let us first begin with the address and data bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now the address and data bus, as you can see here,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: you can see these pins AD0, AD1, AD2 till AD14 here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And then after AD15, AD16, AD17, AD19.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So from 0, from AD0 to this AD19, you have got a total of 20 pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: You have got a total of 20 pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And you already know that the address bus of 8086 is of 20 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So the address is usually kept on these pins from AD0 to this AD19.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this is used for address bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now data bus, it is of 16 bits because 8086 is a 16 bit microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So you do not have separate data pins here because that will again complicate,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: that will again increase the size of this 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And address bus is seldom used in comparison to the data bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Address bus is not frequently used in comparison to the data bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And we have seen why is it so in 8085 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because at the beginning of read or write operation from memory or input output,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: in the T1 clock cycle only, the address buses, they will contain the address.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And after that, that address might not be required.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So from T2, T3, T4 clock cycles, you will have data on these address buses.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So in 8086 CPU also, we have multiplexed the address and data bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So you can see here from AD0 to AD15, you have this notation of AD.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: AD stands for address as well as data.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: However, after this AD15, you have got only A16, A17, A18 and A19.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Since the address bus is of 20 bits, so you have got from 0 to 19, that is 20 address pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the data bus is only of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So you have got AD0 to AD14 and then AD15.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That means a total of 16 data pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So data and address bus are multiplexed.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the lower order 16 bits of the address bus are treated as data bus.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So this addresses will be floated in the T1 clock cycle.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Probably you have known the meaning of T1 clock cycle from our earlier discussions.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that's why I'm using this terminology.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So from T1 clock cycle, the addresses will be floated onto this.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And in subsequent clock cycles, we will have data which will be floated onto this.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then these pins, A16, A17 and A18.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: When the data is floated onto these pins, these pins, the remaining pins, which are 4 in number, will not be used as data pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because of course, data is only of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So they have got this S3, S4, S5 and S6.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: The interpretation of these is that they will be used to signify some status.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So we will talk about what these status pins are in a while.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But you see the beauty of multiplexing these address and data lines.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If it would have not been the case, then in 8086 CPU, the design part would have been complicated.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: You have to make a bigger IC as well as the number of ground pins will also increase.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: The cost of this thing will also increase.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And the point on which they have been multiplexed is that address lines are seldom used in comparison to the data lines.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So on that note, these address and data pins have been discussed.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now let us move on to these status signals.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: S3, S4, S5 and S6, which are multiplexed with the higher 4 bits of this address line.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So for this, let us first discuss this S3 and S4 pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So let me just keep the diagram to this side and bring you the status of S4 and S3 pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So now what this S3 and S4 pin will combinedly tell us is summarized in this particular chart.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If you see here S4, S3 and the segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean the microprocessor, if it is dealing with the externally interfaced memory, then since inside the memory, we have got four segments.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: These extra segments, stack segment, code segment and data segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, if you want to know which segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And apart from that, there is also a lot of vacant memory, which is used for different purposes, which we will come to later.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But for now, if you want to know which segment is being used currently, then you have to see these pins.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: S3 and S4.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If S3 and S4, they have a value of 00, you are using extra segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Otherwise, if the value is 01, stack segment, 10, code segment and 11, data segment.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is used to keep a track of that particular thing.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: S3 and S4, right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And remember that apart from these segments, there is a lot of memory which is vacant, which is definitely used for interrupts.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, interrupts like in 8085, we saw that there were a vector interrupts and their locations, they started from 0000 and 008, then 00.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean, like that, there were some specified address locations at which you used to keep your programs.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, similarly, that thing here is formally called as interrupt to vector table.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, there are specific locations for that and there you will be writing your programs.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, those locations are already reserved in 8086 also.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, we will come to them a little later.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But now, let us discuss the purpose of the other pins that we have got in this thing.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: That is, we have got this pin number S5 and pin number S6.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, what is the purpose of using these pins S5 and S6?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, S5 pin that you see here is interrupt enable flag status.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean, this 8086 microprocessor is also capable of handling interrupts.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, there is a flag which is used inside 8086 CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that IF or the interrupt enable flag, if it is on, it can be known by this S5 pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If this pin has a high value, then that can be treated as interrupt enable flag is on.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And if it has got a low value, that flag is disabled.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And that flag is especially used for maskable interrupts.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: The interrupts which you can deny servicing.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that flag is used for those purposes.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this pin is being used to indicate the status of that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, this is again this S6 pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: S6 pin is used for indicating the status.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We will see that some external device, whether it is input output device or some other processor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If it wants to gain the control of the internal buses, address and data buses of this microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If it wants to gain the control of the internal buses, then this S6 pin will be floated high.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, the bus master can take the control.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that is indicated by this S6 pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, here you can see that we have also discussed these status pins S3, S4, S5 and S6.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, we have discussed these address lines and data lines that you can see on this particular site.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, most of the pins on this particular site have been discussed.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We will come to these pins later on where we will discuss interrupts.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And now, let us again move on to this BHE bar slash S7 pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this BHE bar is actually used to indicate that bus high enable.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: BHE means bus high enable.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, what is this used for?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We already know that externally interfaced memory is 1 megabyte in its maximum locations.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And every location is of 8 bits or 1 byte.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, the addresses that you have in the external memory will be like 0000, 00001, 00002.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: No, not like that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: They will be now in 20 bits.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, you will have an address 5 times 0.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then you will have 00001, 00002, etc.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, in hexadecimal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, there are some odd addresses and some even addresses.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this bus high enable, this bus high enable is used to indicate that odd addresses have been selected or not.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, what happens is the externally interfaced memory of your 8086 is treated as a memory comprised of odd addresses and even addresses.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Which every memory is.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But then, this bus high enable signal is used to indicate that you have got an externally interfaced memory which is treated as an odd memory bank and an even memory bank.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Which corresponds to odd addresses and even addresses.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, if you want to activate, if you want to activate the odd addresses, this signal will be enabled.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This signal will be made as high.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I will later on tell you what this odd and even memory bank means and why is it important.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But for now, you can just understand that the externally interfaced memory of 8086 microprocessor is organized as even bank and odd bank.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And to select the odd bank, this bus high enable signal is being used.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, I will elaborate on this portion a little later.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Maybe in the next video lecture.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And this S7 does not mean anything.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It is reserved.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: It is a spare.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, it does not mean anything.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this pin actually is only meant for this bus high enable.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, we already know the meaning of this minimum and maximum mode pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, there is nothing special in that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, let's come to this read pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this read pin is similar to the pin that we have used in 8085 microprocessor also.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this read pin will tell us if the value of this is 0.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then that means the microprocessor is trying to read something from the external memory.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because a bar is placed over this.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this simply means that it is trying to read something.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If it is 0, it is activated.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, microprocessor is reading something from the external memory.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that will be indicated by this particular pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, now after this read pin, let's now directly come to this ready pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: After this read, I am directly jumping to ready pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We will discuss these two set of pins separately when we will discuss the maximum and minimum

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: mode.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, now this ready pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Ready pin is actually used.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This ready pin is the input that informs the processor that the selected memory or the input output device

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: is ready to complete the data transfer.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Then, ready signal is often used to synchronize the fast processor with slow memory or slow input output device.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, what happens is if this ready pin is high.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This is, you have to supply an input signal at it.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean, this pin is definitely treated as an input pin to the microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If you put a high value at this particular pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: In that case, it indicates that the externally interfaced device or memory, whatever external device is there, it is ready to transfer the data.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because there may be some devices which are slower than this microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This microprocessor operates on 5 megahertz frequency.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: There might be devices which are slower in comparison to that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, to be able to synchronize things between these two properly, we have got this ready pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And this ready pin is actually an input signal to this particular microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And if the value at this pin is 0, then what happens is microprocessor will introduce additional bus idle cycles in their timing diagram.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: We have already seen timing diagrams for 8085.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And there we know that for read or write, some T states are required.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, if a slower device is connected here, then that will, if this pin is 0, if the value at this pin is 0 from that particular device, if it is inserted as so, then if your microprocessor is trying to read something or write something to that particular device,

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: then if the status at this pin is 0, the microprocessor will understand that it needs more time because it is slower.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, it will introduce more bus idle cycles.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If it is doing the read cycle or the write cycle, it is of specific number of T cycles.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, there it will increase its extent.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Instead of taking it regularly, it will introduce additional bus idle cycles.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So that when the device is ready, it will be able to read the data.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is the usage of this ready pin here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, let me first discuss this INTR pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Interrupt pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this interrupt pin is an externally given interrupt.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: But the interrupts that you give on this particular pin are maskable in nature.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: I mean, there is an interrupt flag inside this 8086 CPU.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, in that interrupt flag, if there is an interrupt request which has come from the external world to the microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is also an input signal to the microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: If there is an interrupt request which has come to the microprocessor, then in that case, this microprocessor can serve that interrupt request or deny that.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Depending on whether the interrupt flag is on or off.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is a maskable interrupt which is externally given to this microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: INTR.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Similarly, NMI.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: NMI that you see here is a non-maskable interrupt.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, non-maskable interrupt means irrespective of whatever is the status of interrupt flag inside the microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This NMI, if it is high, this request has to be served.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: One more point of difference between INTR and NMI is INTR is level triggered.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: However, NMI happens to be edge triggered.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is level triggered and this is edge triggered.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this is also one of the points of differences here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Now, let's discuss this test signal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: This test signal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Test signal, it is actually used when we are using multiple processors in the system.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, if you are using a 8087 coprocessor, MAT coprocessor with this processor, then this test signal is actually coupled with this another signal.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this test signal, it will be used with that particular weight instruction.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: And this test signal is usually connected to the busy pin of 8087 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, if you have 8087 microprocessor, which is the MAT coprocessor, it is usually connected to 8086.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this test pin here, it is connected to the busy pin of that for a proper synchronization between these two devices.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Because from this device, if you will give a command to calculate sinusoidal value of something.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, it will return the value after calculating.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, this test pin is connected to the busy pin of that 8087 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that will help achieve a proper synchronization.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, that is why this test pin is being used here.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: Right?

chunks.text: So, now let's talk about this reset pin.

chunks.text: Right?

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, similarly in those days, we had this reset pin.

chunks.title: Video 12 - 8086  Pin Diagram
chunks.text: So, on this pin, if you apply a signal 1, that is plus 1 or plus 5 volt, which is logic 1, for maximum of 4 T states.

chunks.text: Right?

chunks.text: So, this microprocessor will restart.
